Customer to provide representative prompt set (50 prompts) and sample traffic profile by 2025-04-09
Schedule pilot benchmark window for 2025-04-14 09:00-11:00 PT

Samir (SE): prepare model variants and quantization profiles for test (7B/13B int8) by 2025-04-12

meeting_header:
Date: 2025-04-07
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Navarro (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Product), Priya Singh (Quasar Eng Lead), Mark O'Connell (Quasar SRE), Hannah Li (Quasar ML Infra)
summary: POC scoping focused on defining latency SLOs (Time-to-first-token vs Time-per-token), throughput targets, and a concrete measurement/benchmark plan. Agreed on test harness, warm vs cold scenarios, and acceptance criteria. Next steps around sharing scripts and scheduling a 2-hour benchmark window.
topics: SLO definitions (TTFT vs TPOT); percentile targets (p95/p99); warm-up/warm cache considerations; synthetic vs production traffic; payload sizes and token lengths; concurrency and batching; measurement instrumentation (client vs server timestamps); test windows and success criteria.
transcript:
[00:00] Alex (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call...
[00:07] Priya (Quasar): Hey, thanks, uh thanks Alex. We are excited to scope the POC.
[00:15] Samir (SE): Great. Our goal today is to lock down what you want to measure: TTFT vs TPOT, p95/p99 targets, and how we'll run the benchmark.
[00:26] Mark (Quasar SRE): Right, from SRE side we care about tail latency under sustained load. We'll need specifics on payload size and concurrency.
[00:34] Jordan (Product): Also want to capture functional success — correctness/regeneration rate — but we'll treat that as separate evals. Today is performance focused.
[00:42] Priya: Ideal outcome is we can prove our user-facing chat responses hit sub-300ms first character 95% of the time, and throughput to handle 120 QPS peak with 200ms average per-token.
[00:55] Alex: Okay, let's talk terms: TTFT (time-to-first-token) is client-observable latency until first token starts streaming. TPOT (time-per-output-token) is time between token emissions or effective per-token throughput. Sometimes teams conflate token generation latency with model compute per step.
[01:12] Samir: For measurement we'll run three scenarios: cold start (model spin-up), warm steady-state with KV/prefix cache primed, and stress ramp (increasing concurrency). We'll capture both client-side and server-side timestamps.
[01:28] Hannah (ML Infra): What do you mean by server-side timestamps — are you instrumenting inside the runtime?
[01:33] Samir: Yes, runtime emits timestamp events: request-received, first-token-sent, token-n-th-sent. We'll also log GPU utilization and batch sizes.
[01:44] Priya: How do you suggest we shape the traffic? Real chat traffic is very spiky — small prompts, some long context.
[01:50] Samir: We need a representative prompt set. For the bench we'll use a 50-prompt corpus Priya provides with token-length distribution. Then run: 1) single-request latency (10-30 runs) 2) sustained throughput: steady QPS for 10 minutes 3) spike tests with bursts and cooldowns.
[02:07] Mark: For p95/p99 targets, do we measure TTFT only, or TPOT too? We need both for different SLAs.
[02:13] Alex: Recommended acceptance criteria from our side: TTFT p95 <= 250ms, p99 <= 500ms for warm steady-state on the preferred dedicated config. TPOT (effective) p95 <= 35ms per token, p99 <= 75ms per token for sequences after the first token. These numbers are initial proposals — we can tune vs your traffic.
[02:35] Priya: 250ms p95 TTFT sounds promising. Our product goal was 300ms but lower is better.
[02:40] Hannah: Are those for a 7B quantized model or a 13B? We run heavier variants in prod.
[02:46] Samir: We'll test model variants: 7B int8, 13B int8, and a float16 13B if you want. Document will include config. Different models will shift TTFT/TPOT; we'll report per-variant.
[02:58] Jordan: Important to separate cold start SLOs — warm TTFT is what we use for steady SLA, cold start can be relaxed — e.g., 2–5s.
[03:06] Mark: On instrumentation, can we get per-request trace IDs in the logs to join traces with your console?
[03:11] Samir: Yes, we'll include trace ID and hooks to export to your tracing system.
[03:18] Alex: Measurement plan specifics: we'll run an initial smoke test, then a controlled 2-hour window where Redwood runs five 10-minute steady-state tests at target QPS and a 30-minute ramp test. We'll capture CPU/GPU, network, batching, and queueing times.
[03:33] Priya: What's your recommended target QPS for our stated 120 peak?
[03:37] Samir: For 120 peak, test steady-state at 80% (96 QPS) and at 120 QPS, and then stress to 200 QPS to understand graceful degradation.
[03:44] Alex: Also confirm tokenization path: are you sending full context each time or using prefix caching? That affects TTFT.
[03:50] Priya: We'll simulate both: full context for isolation and cached prefix for real user flows.
[03:55] Mark: Any tooling preferences? We use k6 internally; do you support that?
[03:59] Samir: We have a Locust harness plus an internal runner that simulates streaming protocols. We can convert k6 scripts; send one and we'll adapt.
[04:06] Priya: About p95 vs p99 — product wants p95 targets for UX, SRE wants p99 for incident thresholds.
[04:12] Jordan: We'll capture both and provide separate dashboards. p95 guides baseline, p99 informs mitigation and autoscaling.
[04:19] Mark: How do we account for batching variability? Large batches reduce per-token but increase first-token latency.
[04:24] Samir: We'll test with different batching profiles: max latency-focused (small batch sizes), throughput-focused (large dynamic batching), and a hybrid config. We'll report batch size distributions and how they correlate with observed TTFT/TPOT.
[04:37] Priya: For metrics, provide both client-observed (end-to-end) and server-side breakdown: network, preprocess, kv cache lookup, kernel compute, token emit latencies.
[04:48] Alex: Agreement: acceptance criteria to include both E2E and internal breakdowns. Also we'll define a regression threshold — if p95 TTFT degrades >20% vs baseline, alert.
[04:58] Hannah: For warm-up how long do you need to prime KV cache?
[05:02] Samir: Typically a 10–15 minute warm-up with repeated prompts that mimic distribution gets KV/prefix caches in stable state. We'll run a 15-minute warm-up before steady-state tests.
[05:13] Priya: Can you run tests in our VPC/private environment? Data residency constraints require that.
[05:18] Alex: Yes, Redwood Private or Dedicated test slot is possible; SE will coordinate networking. We'll need firewall rules and maybe a temporary test key.
[05:27] Mark: On reporting, we want CSVs and dashboards plus raw traces.
[05:30] Samir: We'll provide dashboards, raw logs (trace IDs), and a summary CSV with per-run p50/p95/p99 TTFT and per-token TPOT.
[05:39] Priya: What's the expected timeline?
[05:42] Alex: If we get prompts by 2025-04-09 and scripts by 04-10, Redwood can run the benchmark 2025-04-14, and deliver initial results within 48 hours.
[05:51] Priya: Sounds good. One more thing, do you account for network jitter from client side?
[05:56] Samir: We'll run tests from both our colocated runner and from within your VPC to isolate network variance. We'll report median network delta.
[06:05] Jordan: Also we'll include a 'cost per 1M tokens' estimate for each config so you can balance latency vs cost.
[06:12] Priya: Yes, finance will ask.
[06:14] Alex: Alright let's do a quick recap of action items and acceptance criteria.
[06:18] Samir: Recap: benchmarks: single-request, 10-minute steady-state, 30-minute ramp; warm-up 15 minutes. Acceptance TTFT p95 <= 250ms p99 <= 500ms (warm), TPOT p95 <= 35ms p99 <= 75ms. Test at 96 QPS, 120 QPS, and 200 QPS stress.
[06:36] Priya: And document model variants plus quantization levels.
[06:40] Alex: Next steps — Alex will share the harness/runbook; Priya will share prompts and traffic profile; Samir will prep model configs. Schedule benchmark on 2025-04-14.
[06:52] Mark: Okay thanks all.
[06:54] Priya: Thanks everyone.
[06:56] Alex: We'll follow up in email with links. Bye.
[15:00] [long discussion: SE ran through batching matrix and quantization tradeoffs; several deep technical questions from Quasar infra team — details logged in SE notes] 
[30:12] [experiment planning: list of 8 test permutations created (model variant x batching x cache state x QPS); references to internal docs and spreadsheets] 
[45:00] [networking and VPC prep conversation; note to Mark: open port 443 to Redwood test runner IPs, temporary key rotation plan] 
[57:00] Alex: Final check — everyone aligned on acceptance criteria and dates?
[57:10] Priya: Yes, we'll deliver prompts by 04-09 and confirm network by 04-11.
[57:20] Samir: We'll be ready to execute on 04-14 and post results within 48 hours.
[57:30] Jordan: We'll include cost estimates and per-variant dashboards.
[57:45] Alex: Great, thanks all.
[57:58] End of call (approx.)
